stitches.name: Chain
stitches.summary: The starting row and the height builder: a run of linked loops worked straight from a slip knot.

instructions.instruction: Make a slip knot and slide it onto the hook, loose enough that the hook still turns freely.
Hold the tail below the hook and wrap the working yarn over the hook from back to front.
Draw that wrap through the loop already on the hook to finish one chain.
Repeat the wrap and the draw through for every chain the pattern asks for, keeping each loop the same size.
Count the V shapes along the front of the chain and never count the loop still on the hook.

stitches.name: Slip stitch
stitches.summary: A flat, nearly invisible stitch that joins a round or travels across the work without adding height.

instructions.instruction: Insert the hook under both top loops of the next stitch.
Wrap the working yarn over the hook from back to front.
Draw that wrap through the stitch and through the loop on the hook in one movement.
One loop is left on the hook and the join lies flat, with no post standing beneath it.
To close a round, work the slip stitch into the first stitch of that same round.

stitches.name: Single crochet
stitches.summary: The shortest basic stitch. It builds dense, sturdy fabric and the tight rounds amigurumi needs.

instructions.instruction: Insert the hook front to back under both top loops of the next stitch.
Yarn over and draw a loop back through the stitch, leaving two loops on the hook.
Yarn over again and draw through both loops on the hook.
One loop remains, and the finished stitch stands a single loop tall.
At the end of a row, chain one and turn before working the next row.

stitches.name: Half double crochet
stitches.summary: A middle-height stitch made by yarning over before the hook enters. It works up fast and drapes softly.

instructions.instruction: Yarn over once before the hook enters anything, and keep that wrap on the shaft.
Insert the hook under both top loops of the next stitch.
Yarn over and pull up a loop, leaving three loops on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through all three loops at once.
The finished stitch sits between a single crochet and a double crochet in height.
Chain two and turn to start a new row of half double crochet.

stitches.name: Double crochet
stitches.summary: The everyday tall stitch behind most blankets and garments. It grows quickly into open, airy fabric.

instructions.instruction: Yarn over once, then insert the hook under both top loops of the next stitch.
Yarn over and pull up a loop so that three loops sit on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through the first two loops on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through the last two loops to close the stitch.
Chain three and turn to bring the next row up to double crochet height.

stitches.name: Treble crochet
stitches.summary: A tall stitch begun with two yarn overs and closed two loops at a time, for long posts and open fabric.

instructions.instruction: Yarn over twice before inserting the hook, so two wraps rest on the shaft.
Insert the hook under both top loops of the next stitch, yarn over, and pull up a loop.
Yarn over and draw through the first two of the four loops now on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through two more, then yarn over and draw through the last two.
Chain four and turn to start a new row of treble crochet.
Every extra starting yarn over adds one more post height and one more closing pair.

stitches.name: Single crochet increase
stitches.summary: Two single crochet worked into one stitch, widening the row or round by exactly one stitch.

instructions.instruction: Work one single crochet into the next stitch as usual and leave it in place.
Insert the hook into that very same stitch again, under both of its top loops.
Work a second complete single crochet there, closing it the same way as the first.
The pair shares one base, so the stitch count for the row or round rises by one.
In the round, spacing increases evenly keeps the fabric from cupping or ruffling.

stitches.name: Single crochet two together
stitches.summary: A decrease that gathers two neighboring stitches into one single crochet, lowering the count by one.

instructions.instruction: Insert the hook into the next stitch, yarn over, and pull up a loop.
Leave that loop on the hook and insert the hook into the following stitch.
Yarn over and pull up a second loop, so three loops sit on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through all three loops to finish one stitch.
Two stitches now share one top, so the count falls by one.

stitches.name: Double crochet two together
stitches.summary: A double crochet decrease that leaves each half unfinished, then closes both halves into one stitch.

instructions.instruction: Yarn over, insert the hook into the next stitch, yarn over, and pull up a loop.
Yarn over and draw through two loops only, stopping with two loops on the hook.
Repeat that unfinished double crochet in the following stitch, ending with three loops.
Yarn over and draw through all three loops to join the pair into one stitch.
Leaving each half unfinished is what lets a decrease work at any stitch height.

stitches.name: Back loop only
stitches.summary: A placement change: work each stitch under the back loop alone to leave a ridge and stretchy fabric.

instructions.instruction: Look at the top of the next stitch and find its two loops, front and back.
The back loop is the one farther away from you as you face the work.
Insert the hook under that back loop alone, skipping the front loop entirely.
Complete whichever stitch the pattern names in the usual way.
The unworked front loops line up as a visible ridge, which is how ribbing is made.

stitches.name: Magic ring
stitches.summary: An adjustable start for working in the round that pulls closed, leaving no hole at the center.

instructions.instruction: Wrap the yarn around two fingers, crossing the working yarn over the tail to form a loop.
Slide the loop off, insert the hook, and pull up a loop of working yarn through it.
Chain one to secure the ring, then work the round's stitches over both strands of the loop.
Make the stitch count the pattern asks for, sliding them together so the ring stays flexible.
Pull the short tail firmly to draw the center closed before joining or continuing in a spiral.

stitches.name: Fasten off
stitches.summary: The finishing step that locks the last stitch and secures the yarn end so the work cannot unravel.

instructions.instruction: Finish the final stitch so that only one loop is left on the hook.
Cut the working yarn, leaving a tail of at least six inches to weave in.
Yarn over with the cut end and draw it all the way through that last loop.
Pull the tail snug to lock the stitch, then slide the hook out.
Thread the tail on a blunt needle and weave it through several stitches on the wrong side.
